name: Idiomatic Go
description: Go-specific idioms and best practices. Effective Go, the Go proverbs, and community conventions.

rules.name: Accept Interfaces, Return Structs
rules.instruction: Function parameters should accept interfaces; return types should be concrete structs. This maximizes flexibility for callers while keeping the contract clear.

rules.name: Errors Are Values
rules.instruction: Handle errors explicitly with if err != nil checks. Never panic for expected failure modes. Use error wrapping (fmt.Errorf with %w) to add context. Define sentinel errors or custom types for errors callers need to inspect.

rules.name: Small Interfaces
rules.instruction: Define interfaces with one to three methods. The larger the interface, the weaker the abstraction. Define interfaces at the point of use (consumer side), not at the point of implementation.

rules.name: Package by Responsibility
rules.instruction: Package names are short, lowercase, singular nouns that describe what the package provides (buffer, editor, session), not what it contains (utils, helpers, common).

rules.name: Zero Values Are Useful
rules.instruction: Design types so their zero value is valid and useful. A zero-value sync.Mutex is ready to use. A zero-value bytes.Buffer is an empty buffer. Follow this convention.

rules.name: Composition Over Embedding
rules.instruction: Prefer named fields over embedding when you do not want to promote all methods. Embedding is for interface satisfaction and method forwarding, not for code reuse.

rules.name: Goroutines Must Have an Owner
rules.instruction: Every goroutine must have a clear owner responsible for stopping it. Use context cancellation, done channels, or sync.WaitGroup. Never fire-and-forget a goroutine.

rules.name: Channel Semantics
rules.instruction: Use channels for communication and coordination between goroutines. Use mutexes for protecting shared state. Do not use channels as mutexes or mutexes as channels.

rules.name: Table-Driven Tests
rules.instruction: Use table-driven tests with t.Run subtests. Each case is a struct with inputs and expected outputs. Use t.Helper() on test helpers. No test framework dependencies — stdlib only.

rules.name: Doc Comments on Exports
rules.instruction: Every exported type, function, method, and constant must have a doc comment starting with the name. Comments are complete sentences. No exported symbol goes undocumented.

rules.name: No Init Functions
rules.instruction: Avoid init() functions. They run implicitly, complicate testing, and create hidden dependencies. Use explicit initialization in main() or constructors.

rules.name: Use the Standard Library
rules.instruction: Prefer stdlib over third-party packages when the stdlib solution is adequate. Never reimplement functionality available in the standard library.
